children.name: Project Description
children.reason:
Evaluation of the README file:

project_purpose:
Score (avg): 3.0
[CODING] The README gives only a partial picture of the project's purpose. It opens with a logo and the title "Smart Village App - Main-Server" and states: "This main-server is one main part of the whole Smart Village App project. For more information visit https://github.com/ikuseiGmbH/smart-village-app." It also invites the reader to "visit the german website to get in touch with us and present your ideas and visions: https://smart-village.app." However, it never explains what the Smart Village App actually does or what the main-server is responsible for. The purpose can only be inferred indirectly from later sections: a "GraphQL API" served at /graphiql, a "User management" area at /accounts with permission assignment, and example documents such as `doc/poi_mutation_example.graphql` (entities like POIs). No feature list, use cases, target audience, or high-level architecture description is provided, and the reader is instead redirected to external links. This makes the purpose understandable at a rough level but far from self-contained, which justifies a neutral score.

setup_instructions:
Score (avg): 4.0
[CODING] The README contains a substantial "Setup process" section that walks through most of the necessary steps: (1) "Ruby installation" with macOS/brew-specific commands (`ruby-install 2.6.8`, `export CFLAGS=...`, `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`), (2) "Bundler installation" (`gem install bundler -v '2.3.20'`), "Master key configuration" (`config/master.key`), "Database configuration" with a full example `config/database.yml` (mysql2 adapter, utf8mb4, pool, socket, development/test database names), "Database and user setup" (`rake db:create db:migrate`, `rake db:seed`, and a Rails console snippet to set a password), "Run the server locally" (`rails s`), and "Login" instructions (http://localhost:4000 with "admin@smart-village.app"). It also explains that permissions must be assigned at http://localhost:4000/accounts or login fails with "Error! E-Mail oder Passwort ist falsch." A "Tech Stack" section lists Ruby 2.6.8 and Rails 5.2.4. Points are deducted because the instructions are not fully polished or complete: several prerequisites are never mentioned (installing MySQL, Redis/Elasticsearch or other services, `bundle install` itself is never explicitly run), the numbering is broken ("#### 1. Ru the following commands" contains a typo, then jumps to "#### 3." without a step 2), the GraphQL example references `doc/poi_mutation_example.graphql` twice where a second, different file was presumably intended, the setup is macOS-centric without ENV/deployment notes, and the document ends with an unclosed code fence after the "Tech Stack" list, suggesting truncation.

info_project_status:
Score (avg): 1.0
[CODING] The README contains no statement about the project's development or maintenance status. There is no mention of whether the project is in active development, feature-frozen, in maintenance mode, deprecated, or no longer maintained. It carries only Code Climate badges for "Maintainability" and "Test Coverage" hosted at `codeclimate.com/github/ikuseiGmbH/smart-village-app-mainserver`, plus a link to the German website for contact — none of which communicate lifecycle status. There is also no version/release information, no roadmap, no changelog reference, and no notice about supported versions (the only version hints are the EOL "Ruby version: 2.6.8" and "Rails version: 5.2.4" in the Tech Stack section, presented as facts rather than status information). Consequently, a reader cannot determine the project's current state from the README at all.

info_maintainer:
Score (avg): 2.0
[CODING] Maintainer information is only implicit. The Code Climate badge URLs point to the GitHub account `ikuseiGmbH` (`codeclimate.com/github/ikuseiGmbH/smart-village-app-mainserver`), and the purpose section links to `https://github.com/ikuseiGmbH/smart-village-app` and to `https://smart-village.app`, which gives a reasonable hint that ikuseiGmbH is the organization behind the project. The README also says "Please visit the german website to get in touch with us and present your ideas and visions," which opens a channel for contact/contribution. However, there is no explicit statement naming a maintainer, no "Contributing" section, no CONTRIBUTING.md reference, no code of conduct, no issue/PR guidelines, no list of authors or core contributors, and no explanation of how the community can participate. The maintainership must therefore be inferred from badge URLs rather than being described, so the score is low but not the minimum.

children.name: Project Structure
children.reason:
Project structure evaluation:

directory_organization:
Score (avg): 5.0
[CODING] This is a Rails 5/6-era application and it follows the framework's canonical layout almost perfectly. All application code lives under `app/` with the standard subdirectories (`assets/`, `channels/`, `controllers/`, `graphql/`, `helpers/`, `jobs/`, `mailers/`, `models/`, `services/`, `views/`); framework configuration is in `config/` (including `environments/`, `initializers/`, `locales/`); database artifacts are in `db/` with a timestamped `migrate/` directory, plus `schema.rb` and `seeds.rb`; tests are in `spec/`; Rake extensions in `lib/tasks/`; documentation and sample payloads in `doc/` (GraphQL mutation examples, GTFS CSVs, `waste_types.json`); and deployment assets isolated in `docker/` (`database.yml`, `entrypoint.sh`, `nginx.conf`, `unicorn.rb`) plus `Dockerfile`/`docker-compose*.yml`. Static deliverables are correctly placed in `public/` (`mobile-app/configs/*.json`, `mobile-app/contents/*.html`, `404.html`). Nothing of substance is misplaced (e.g., no business logic or bespoke scripts dumped at the repository root beyond the expected `Rakefile`, `Gemfile`, `config.ru`). This matches the expected conventions for the technology stack extremely well.

naming_conventions:
Score (avg): 5.0
[CODING] Naming is consistent with Ruby/Rails conventions throughout: `snake_case` for all Ruby files (`app/models/data_resources/resource_modules/accessibility_information.rb`, `app/graphql/resolvers/points_of_interest_search.rb`, `app/jobs/send_single_push_notification_job.rb`), pluralized controller names mapped to resources (`app_user_contents_controller.rb`, `static_contents_controller.rb`), `*_spec.rb` for tests mirroring the source path, `*.html.erb` / `*.json.jbuilder` / `*.ics.erb` view suffixes indicating format, `*.yml` for configuration, dotted conventions like `.eslintrc.json`/`.rubocop.yml`/`.codeclimate.yml`, and `*.rake` in `lib/tasks`. Migration files use the standard `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_snake_case_description.rb` pattern and the vendored `acts_as_taggable_on` migrations correctly retain their engine-qualified suffixes. Only trivial blemishes exist: `spec/factories/adresses.rb` is a misspelling of "addresses" (while the model spec is correctly named `address_spec.rb`), and a few files mix stacked suffixes such as `waste_location_type_type.rb` or `i18n_json.rb`. These are cosmetic and do not break the otherwise uniform snake_case convention.

separation_of_concerns:
Score (avg): 5.0
[CODING] Concerns are cleanly separated by directory: source code (`app/`), tests (`spec/`), configuration (`config/`, `.rubocop.yml`, `.eslintrc.json`, `.rspec`, `.codeclimate.yml`), CI pipeline definitions (`.gitlab-ci.yml`, `.gitlab-ci.yml.tmpl`), schema/migrations (`db/`), deployment (`docker/`, `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose*.yml`, `stack.yml`), and documentation (`doc/`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `LICENSES_REPORT.md`). Within `app/` the Rails concerns are also separated: persistence in `models/`, request handling in `controllers/`, HTTP-facing schema in `graphql/` (further split into `mutations/`, `resolvers/`, `types/`), reusable business logic in `services/` (`push_notification.rb`, `weather_map_service.rb`, `gtfs_redis_adapter.rb`), background work in `jobs/`, email in `mailers/` with matching templates in `views/mailers/`, and shared, cross-cutting code in `concerns/` (`sortable.rb`, `searchable.rb`, `filter_by_role.rb` for models; `sortable_controller.rb` for controllers). Secrets are also separated from configuration via `config/credentials.yml.enc` and a `credentials.yml.tmpl` placeholder rather than committing real credentials.

modularity:
Score (avg): 4.0
[CODING] The codebase is broken into coherent, domain-aligned modules rather than flat catch-all folders. `app/models/data_resources/` groups the content types (`attraction.rb`, `event_record.rb`, `news_item.rb`, `point_of_interest.rb`, `tour.rb`, `waste*.rb`) and further decomposes shared value objects into `resource_modules/` (`address.rb`, `contact.rb`, `media_content.rb`, `opening_hour.rb`, `price.rb`, `region.rb`, `web_url.rb`, `public_transportation/travel_time.rb`), with dedicated sub-packages for `notification/`, `survey/`, and `waste/`. The GraphQL layer is similarly decomposed: one file per operation in `mutations/` and `resolvers/`, plus `types/input_types/` and `types/query_types/` (with a nested `query_types/public_transportation/`), and shared bases (`base_object.rb`, `base_input_object.rb`, `base_interface.rb`). Services are single-purpose classes (`category_service.rb`, `clean_up_service.rb`, `recurring_dates_for_event_service.rb`, `public_transportation/import_service.rb`). Points are withheld for some duplication and overlap: `mutations/vote_for_survey.rb` and `mutations/votes_for_survey.rb` are near-identical sibling operations, and the same application views are duplicated under both `views/doorkeeper/applications/` and `views/oauth/applications/` with corresponding controllers in `controllers/oauth/applications_controller.rb`. Some larger modules also look like they may be doing more than one thing (e.g. `app/models/data_resources/generic_item.rb` plus `generic_item/message.rb` alongside `models/static_content.rb` and `models/notification.rb` at the top level), suggesting a slightly uneven boundary between the `data_resources/` namespace and the flat `models/` root.
